visual.method: In-app browser (Claude desktop) with viewport emulation at the exact declared sizes; overflow measured as documentElement.scrollWidth minus clientWidth and by scanning every element bounding box for right edges past the viewport; screenshots inspected at the declared viewport for the first screen and, for the remainder of the page, at the same width with the height extended to the full document height (layout depends on width only; the stylesheet uses no viewport-height units except body min-height). No image artifacts retained. The stylesheet and markup bytes inspected are the ones recorded above; the only source change after the screenshot inspection was JavaScript (the clipboard fallback), re-measured for overflow at both viewports afterwards.

Control strip sits above the stacked title; intro and public notice stack; cards, input, textarea, stacked action buttons, issue link, and omissions list stay inside the viewport; long manifest JSON wraps inside the textarea. observations: The in-app browser pane reported document.hidden === true for the whole session, so requestAnimationFrame never fires there. None of the fifteen closure files uses requestAnimationFrame (grep over the closure), so no layout pass on this page is frame-gated and nothing here was frame-timed; the pane is not a surface for the public-feedback-interaction performance baseline.

Clipboard: in the hidden pane navigator.clipboard.writeText rejects with NotAllowedError. FeedbackManifestRuntime.js originally fell back to select-for-manual-copy only when writeText was absent, so the rejection was unhandled and the status line never changed. Fixed the same day under operator direction: a rejected writeText now takes the same fallback as an absent one. Measured in the pane after the fix: no unhandled rejection, textarea focused with its full contents selected, status set to the manual-copy message.
Accessibility floor lowered from 42 to 32 CSS px in the contract by operator decision on 2026-09-06, because the shared control strip is 32 px by design; see the profile rationale.
